name: FASER / FASERnu
summary: FASER studies very forward particles at the LHC. Its FASERnu tungsten-emulsion target and electronic spectrometer have established collider-neutrino observations and enabled high-energy neutrino-interaction measurements.
physics_targets: TeV-scale neutrino interactions and flavour-dependent cross sections
Forward hadron production in proton collisions
detection_principle: Neutrinos from hadron decays at ATLAS traverse rock and interact in dense material 480 m downstream. Emulsion films resolve interaction vertices and lepton signatures; scintillators, silicon tracking and a magnetic spectrometer identify penetrating muons and reconstruct electronic events.

sites.name: Switzerland; TI12 tunnel at the CERN LHC, downstream in the forward direction from ATLAS
sites.location: Switzerland; TI12 tunnel at the CERN LHC, downstream in the forward direction from ATLAS

status.label: Run 3 exposure complete / analysis and future preparations
status.evidence: The LHC entered Long Shutdown 3 on 29 June 2026, so the 2026-10 archive snapshot must not imply ongoing collider data taking. FASER analysis and future-detector development continue.

phases.name: LHC Run 3 FASER / FASERnu

phases.name: FASERnu2 at the proposed FPF
phases.description: Proposed successor emulsion detector in the FPF cavern on the French side of CERN. The current official concept has a 20-tonne tungsten target and 3300 emulsion layers. It is distinct from the Run 3 FASERnu target in TI12.

results.summary: Electronic detector observed collider muon-neutrino interactions with high significance.
Reported a calorimeter-based high-energy electron-neutrino analysis, adding a complementary identification method to emulsion studies.

science_scope: The record describes the named experiment as one programme; detector subsystems and repeated analyses are not counted as independent experiments.
